text: Galaxy Research: Crypto VC Funding Rebounds to $5.6 Billion in Q2, Up 31% QoQ Galaxy Research reported that crypto and blockchain venture funding rebounded in Q2 2026 after cooling in the first quarter. VCs invested about $5.6 billion across 384 deals, with capital deployed up 31% quarter-over-quarter and deal count up 10%, driven mainly by later-stage financings. At the first-half pace, full-year 2026 investment would reach about $20.04 billion, slightly below 2025 but above most of 2023 and 2024. Later-stage companies captured 78.3% of total funding in the quarter. Trading, exchange, investing and lending companies led by category with about $3.52 billion, while U.S.-based companies received 73.5% of invested capital. Fundraising for new crypto venture funds remained difficult: only five new funds raised about $3.9 billion in Q2, the lowest quarterly fund count since Q4 2019. — link

text: UK FCA Releases Cryptoasset Regulatory Guidance, Authorization Applications to Open on Sept. 30 The UK's FCA has released guidance on the scope of the country's future cryptoasset regime. The regime will take effect on Oct. 25, 2027, with authorization applications opening on Sept. 30, 2026. The guidance covers qualifying stablecoin issuance, crypto trading platforms, dealing and arranging, custody, and staking services. The FCA will consult on targeted updates in October following recent legislative changes. — link

text: 9 of Top 10 UK Retail Banks Block or Limit Crypto Transactions UK retail banks will not be forced to lift blanket restrictions on payments routed to cryptocurrency exchanges even after the Financial Conduct Authority's (FCA) comprehensive crypto regulatory regime takes effect in October 2027. Despite the UK government's stated ambitions to establish a global digital asset hub and ongoing pressure on lenders, nine out of the top ten UK retail banks currently block or cap crypto-related payments. While the FCA expressed hope that upcoming regulatory safeguards will encourage institutions to voluntarily phase out blanket prohibitions, the regulator confirmed it will not legally compel banks to process crypto transactions, leaving risk appetites entirely at their discretion. — link

text: Fitch: Malaysia Ranks Among Most Open Islamic Crypto Markets as Regulated Volume Tops $4B According to TheStar, Fitch Ratings reported that Malaysia has become one of the most open Islamic markets for cryptocurrencies, driven by clear regulations and Sharia-compliant classifications. Between 2020 and 1H26, the Securities Commission Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council endorsed major crypto assets—including BTC, ETH, XRP, and XLM—as Sharia-compliant, with 10 licensed digital asset entities operating under its regime by mid-2026. In 2025, trading volumes on regulated local exchanges grew 23% year-on-year to surpass $4 billion, representing roughly 2.5% of the domestic equity market, while banking support remains largely confined to transactional services for licensed operators. — link

text: Six Malaysians Sentenced in Singapore Over S$4.9M Crypto & Poker Heist According to Lianhe Zaobao, six Malaysian men were convicted and sentenced in the High Court of Singapore on September 14 for their roles in an armed robbery that occurred in Bukit Timah in 2024, with the two ringleaders each receiving 12 years and 11 months' imprisonment alongside 24 strokes of the cane. Court documents revealed that the perpetrators learned that high-stakes poker games were frequently hosted at a luxury residential property, with players routinely settling wagers in cryptocurrency; the robbers then broke into the premises armed with weapons, coerced players into transferring crypto assets to designated wallets, and looted cash and luxury items valued at ~S$4.906 million in total. To date, police have recovered cryptocurrency valued at around S$1.69 million, while the remainder of the stolen funds and property remains unaccounted for. — link
